content.overview: Daily light integral combines photon intensity with time. Equal DLI can arise from different intensity-duration combinations, so DLI should be interpreted alongside photoperiod, instantaneous intensity and crop/environment context.

vocabulary.definition: The accumulated amount of photosynthetically active photons received per unit area over a day.
The duration of the light period within a 24-hour cycle.
Integrated photon exposure over a defined time interval and area.

sections.title: DLI is PPFD integrated through time
sections.body: Representative PPFD and the actual light duration are both needed. One instantaneous measurement does not describe daily photon exposure.

sections.title: Equal DLI does not mean identical conditions
sections.body: Two schedules may produce similar DLI while using different PPFD and photoperiod. Instantaneous intensity, photoperiod biology and environmental load can still differ.

sections.title: Use crop and system context
sections.body: Higher photon delivery can change heat load, transpiration and irrigation demand. DLI should be reviewed with temperature, humidity, root-zone response and developmental stage.

workedExamples: A lower PPFD for a longer photoperiod can approach the DLI of a higher PPFD for a shorter duration, but the crop does not necessarily experience those schedules identically.
commonMistakes: Treating DLI as independent of photoperiod.
Calculating DLI from the brightest single point.
Copying DLI ranges from another species as a cannabis universal.
content.practicalApplication: Calculate illustrative DLI from representative PPFD and photoperiod, then state the assumptions and why the result does not by itself establish an optimum.
content.summary: DLI is a daily exposure metric, not a universal prescription.
